neighbours.label: the noun of a 'making progress' idiom: headway, strides, inroads, progress
fire: Talks on the new budget made slow headway during the spring.
Researchers have made huge strides in battery storage lately.
The startup is making inroads among rural clinics.
After weeks of effort, the crew finally made some headway on the backlog.
Engineers have made real progress on the water system this year.
The school has made impressive strides in reading scores.
Rival brands have made deep inroads into the local market.
The reforms gained little headway among the older judges.
quiet: Talks on the new budget took place during the spring.
Researchers have bought huge tanks for battery storage lately.
The startup is hiring nurses among rural clinics.
After weeks of effort, the crew finally cleaned out the shed.
Engineers have checked pipes in the water system this year.
The school has painted new signs for the reading room.
Rival brands have sold cheap soap at the local market.
The reforms annoyed most of the older judges.

notes: The direct logit effect agrees: the + output direction suppresses ' advances', ' strides', ' progress', so this pole promotes them.
